title: Parker sleeping in Smith's bed with his shoes on
summary: Parker stayed at Smith's home, slept in his shoes while Smith's wife worked, and left after being told to get a room.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: There's that little story you told me, which is funny, about how you'd be sleeping in the bed with your wife and you let Charlie sleep during the day when you were (?).
But what kind of a guy was it who would use your bed, use your hospitality, but sleep in his bed leaving his shoes on? That wasn't a very nice thing to do.

No. He must have been gettin' off then. But I didn't pay no attention to him because I'd hardly ever see him. I was busy writing music and be gone. And he had to be there all by himself all day. And he just wouldn't pull his shoes off. My wife got to grumbling about it, because she was working herself. She was working in the restaurant. I was off at the Woodside writing music, and she'd be down there at Andy Kirk's restaurant, waiting tables. And she'd come home sometimes, and she'd see him laying up there with his shoes on. Clothes on, too. So she got to squawkin'. So I had to get after him about it. So it wasn't long before he left there.
I mean, he preferred to leave rather than take his shoes off. He didn't see reason about it.
Well, his old lady got to talkin', and she didn't want him there in the first place. She said, 'Charlie, get you a room, so we don't have to (?) in sin. Try to get you a room

somewhere." It was, I think, the next couple of days, that Diz and them made him a little (?) and took it over to Philadelphia and played a show there for about a week. They stayed about a week, and when they got through with it, McShann sent for him to come back to Kansas City.
